name: std_RunPreinitArray
summary: Calls every entry of the CRT pre-initialiser table (0x00799C94..0x0079AA18). Each slot stores an offset relative to its own address, so the runner adds the slot address to the word before calling it - the position-independent form of .preinit_array/.init_array used by the statically linked C++ runtime.
evidence: ResetVector (0x00100000) calls it 5th, after the heap region has been committed by 0x00104400 and before the other two init-list runners. Assembly: push {r4,r5,r6,lr}; ldr r4,[pc,#0x18]; add r4,pc; ldr r5,[pc,#0x18]; add r5,pc; loop: ldr r0,[r4]; add r0,r4; blx r0; adds r4,#4; cmp r4,r5. Literals at 0x00100BBC/0x00100BC0 give 0x00799C94 and 0x0079AA18, i.e. 865 slots (0xD84 bytes). Only caller besides itself: ResetVector.

name: std_RunInitArray
summary: Calls every absolute function pointer between the two bound words at 0x0079AA18 and 0x0079AA1C. In the retail image both bounds hold the same value, so the list is linked empty - it exists for libraries that register static constructors into it at link time.
evidence: ResetVector calls it after std_RunPreinitArray. Body is only `puVar1 = g_0010281c; for (puVar2 = g_00102818; puVar2 < puVar1; puVar2++) (*(code*)*puVar2)();`. Both literal-pool words at 0x00102818/0x0010281C contain 0x0079AA18, and nothing else in the image writes 0x0079AA18 (checked with a full-image pointer scan), so the array is empty in retail.

name: maybe_Os_RunLateBootSetup
summary: Last step of ResetVector: brings up the SDK synchronisation layer (0x001076A8), clamps the committed memory size to zero (0x00104510(0)), creates the application heap (0x00102894(0)) and finishes the allocator setup (0x0010742C). Nothing else calls it, so it is purely a boot-order entry point.
evidence: Only caller is ResetVector (last call). Body: func_001076A8(); func_00104510(0); func_00102894(0); func_0010742C();. 0x00102894 is the heap-creation routine (see its entry); the two remaining calls bracket it, so the sequence reads 'bring up the SDK sync layer -> reset the size limits -> create the heap -> finalise the allocator'.

name: Mem_InitializeMainHeap
summary: Creates the application heap: marks the heap block ready, publishes the heap descriptor at 0x007E790C, then asks 0x00107B54 to reserve heapSize (rounded down to 8) bytes with permission word 0x300 and alignment/type 0xF. On success it maps the block (0x00119BA8/0x0010DD58/0x00119E1C) and returns 0; a non-zero return means the reservation failed.
evidence: Called with 0 from the boot chain (0x00102874). Body writes the 'initialised' byte at *(u8*)(0x007AE910+3), calls 0x00107770(0x007E790C,0x100), then `result = func_00107B54(0x300, heapSize & ~7, 0xf)` and on `result >= 0` runs the map/unmap pair 0x00119BA8 / 0x00119E1C and closes with 0x0010DD58(0). Matches the heap-carving documented in 3DS_Translate/docs/AGENT_GUIDE.md ('the game carves the linear heap into fixed heaps at boot').

name: maybe_Mem_InitAllocatorState
summary: One-time reset of the allocator bookkeeping: clears the descriptor memory, initialises two pool/block allocators (0x007AE4A0 and the two 0x007C86xx blocks), records whether the 'extended memory' probes (0x0010D68C / 0x0010CC00) succeed, and stores the allocator mode returned by 0x00107B1C in the byte at +2.
evidence: No callers - reached only from the init list. Body: func_00116AE0 (memset) over the allocator descriptor; 0x00107894(g,0); 0x00107880(g,0); 0x00111CD8(g_00102b74,1); 0x00111E28 x2 (critical-section init); 0x00111D50(g) (lock); 0x00107EC0(0); `if (0x0010D68C() || 0x0010CC00()) *puVar1 = 1;` then `puVar1[2] = 0x00107B1C()`. The globals it touches (0x007AE4A0, 0x007C865C, 0x007C8668, 0x007AE49C) are the same ones the heap carver 0x00102EF8 and the allocator use.

name: Mem_SetCommittedSize
summary: Grows or shrinks the committed part of the linear heap through svcControlMemory, then records the new size. Growing uses memory operation 3 (commit) with permission 3, shrinking uses operation 1 (free) with permission 0; size must be 4 KiB aligned, otherwise the previous result is returned unchanged.
evidence: `if ((size & 0xfff) == 0) { cur = *(u32*)(state+8); if (cur < size) rc = func_001053D0(&out, cur+0x8000000, 0, size-cur, 3, 3); else rc = func_001053D0(&out, size+0x8000000, 0, cur-size, 1, 0); if (rc >= 0) *(u32*)(state+8) = size; }`. 0x001053D0 is a 6-argument wrapper around svcControlMemory (MEMOP_FREE=1 / MEMOP_COMMIT=3 / MEMOP_PROT=6, 0x8000000 = the process virtual base), also used by 0x00104400 with op 0x10003/3. Called from 0x00104400.

name: Mem_CommitFreeRegion
summary: Commits everything the process may still use: takes the FCRAM size (0x0010439C), subtracts the reserved block (0x001043AC), clamps the committed size to 2 MB via Mem_SetCommittedSize, and then commits or frees the remainder page-aligned so that 0x007AEA7C holds the base and the length of the committed region.
evidence: ResetVector calls it before the init arrays. Body: total=func_0010439C(); reserved=func_001043AC(); func_00104304(0x200000); `want = (total - reserved - 0x200000) & 0xfffff000;` then two svcControlMemory calls (op 0x10003/perm 3 to commit, op 1/perm 0 to free) and the bookkeeping `g_0010450c[1] = want; g_0010450c[0] = out;` (0x007AEA7C).

name: maybe_Os_FetchBootParameter
summary: Caches one word of boot information: if the global at 0x007AF8E4 is still zero it asks the query helper 0x0010B210 for a value and stores the result. Runs before the linear-heap size is measured, so the cached word is most likely the console/memory configuration.
evidence: Body is only `if (*g == 0) { u32 v = 0; if ((func_0010B210(&v) & 0x80000000) == 0) *g = v; }` with g = 0x007AF8E4. Its only caller is 0x00106F70, which immediately measures the linear heap and then sets the heap size, so the value is consumed while sizing memory.

name: Os_InitMemoryManager
summary: Memory-manager boot entry: caches the boot parameter, opens the SDK session, measures the free FCRAM window, sets up thread-local storage, and finally hands the 48 MB (0x03000000) application heap size to 0x0010BDB0. Reached from ResetVector through 0x00113420.
evidence: Body is 0x24 bytes: bl 0x106EC8; bl 0x107010; bl 0x106FFC; bl 0x106F94; bl 0x11697C (returns 0x03000000); then a tail branch to 0x10BDB0 with r0 = 0x03000000. 0x106F94 is the linear-RAM scan, 0x11697C initialises TLS for the main thread. 0x03000000 = 48 MB is exactly the total the AGENT_GUIDE's 44 MB main heap plus the smaller heaps add up to.

name: Mem_ComputeLinearHeapRange
summary: Finds how much of the FCRAM linear heap the application may use: walks svcQueryMemory downwards from 0x0FFFF000 in 4 KiB steps until the block that contains 0x0E000000 is found, then records the range [0x0E000000, top) in the range descriptor at 0x007F2B88.
evidence: `uVar2 = 0x10000000; do { uVar2 -= 0x1000; rc = func_0010B228(&base, &state, uVar2); } while (rc >= 0 && state != 0 && base > 0xe000000); if (uVar2 < 0xe000000) uVar2 = 0xe000000; func_00110C90(0x007F2B88, 0xe000000, uVar2 + 0xf2000000);` - the last argument is the wrap-around form of (top - 0x0E000000). func_00110C90 stores exactly (base, base+size) in the descriptor, i.e. it is the range/allocator descriptor init.

name: Os_IpcCommand2
summary: Submits the fixed request 0x00010002 (command 2, one normal parameter with value 0x20) to the session handle at 0x007AF900 and returns the first response word. Non-negative results are the service's answer; a negative value is the IPC result code.
evidence: Assembly: `mrc p15,0,r4,c13,c0,3` (thread pointer), `ldr r0,[pc,#0x24]` (literal at 0x00107834 = 0x00010002) -> `str r0,[r4,#0x80]!`, `mov r0,#0x20; str r0,[r4,#4]`, `ldr r0,[pc,#0x18]` -> `ldr r0,[r0]` (handle at 0x007AF900), `svc #0x32` (svcSendSyncRequest), then `ldrge r0,[r4,#4]`. 0x00010002 decodes as command 2 with one parameter in the 3DS IPC header layout (bits 0-15 command, 16-20 normal params). Callers: 0x00113420 / 0x00113430, the session bring-up helpers.

name: maybe_Mem_MapSharedBlock
signature: int maybe_Mem_MapSharedBlock(u32 type, u32 size, u32 mode)
summary: Reserves and maps one shared-memory block: lazily opens the session described by 0x007AE910/0x007AE920, asks the service for a block of `size` bytes of the given type (request 0x00010040), keeps the returned handle, records two capability flags from the reply, then maps the block (request 0x00020080) and hands the mode plus the two returned words to 0x0010D6CC. Called with (0x300, size, 0xF) from the heap bootstrap.
evidence: Callers: only 0x00102894 (heap creation), with (0x300, heapSize, 0xf). Body: lazy session open via 0x0010BD94(0x007AE920)/0x0010BD64; 0x0010DDCC (ensure open); 0x0010DC28(&handle,size,&a,&b) -> request 0x00010040, returns a handle plus two words; 0x0010CF40(handle); 0x001143A8(b&1); 0x001143B8((b>>1)&1); 0x0010CD94 (close); 0x0010CD84(type); then 0x0010DBD8(size2,addr2,&x,&y) -> request 0x00020080; 0x0010D6CC(mode,x,y), which N_080 names maybe_Os_OpenServiceHandle - the two readings disagree, so the final step is described only as 'hand the mode and both returned words to 0x0010D6CC'. Errors are reported through 0x00118924 with the file/line literal 0x00107C98.

name: Snd_InitSystemState
summary: Initialises the global sound-system state block once: sets the 'open' flag, stores the default gains (1.0f at +4/+8/+0xC/+0x10 and +0x28/+0x2C), zeroes the per-voice and per-channel tables, allocates the mixing critical sections, then queries the output mode from the audio service and keeps it as 0 = mono, 1 = stereo, 2 = surround in self[3].
evidence: Single caller: 0x00107544, the sound module initialiser, which passes the .bss singleton 0x007EF3C4 and then calls 0x00112A74/0x00112A9C/0x00112D98 (its lock/unlock/set-mode trio) and 0x0010BF58. Body stores the literal 0x3F800000 (1.0f) repeatedly, calls 0x001184F0(&v,1,0x70001) and then maps `v & 0xff` to 0/1/2 (`cVar5 = uVar4 != 0; if (uVar4 == 2) cVar5 = 2;`), which is the 3DS speaker configuration, and closes with 0x00111E28 on the structure at +0x44 (critical section init).

name: Os_CloseIpcSession
summary: Closes the SDK session whose handle lives at 0x007AF0D8 with svcCloseHandle (svc 0x23) and resets the slot to its 'closed' marker. Returns the handle that was open, or the fixed 'not open' result 0xE0A0CFF8 when there was nothing to close; a negative close result is reported through 0x00118924.
evidence: Assembly: `ldr r4,[pc,#0x34]` (literal at 0x0010CDD4 = 0x007AF0D8); `ldr r0,[r4]; cmp r0,#0; ldreq r0,[pc,#0x2c]` (literal 0x0010CDD8 = 0xE0A0CFF8); else `svc #0x23; ldr r1,[pc,#0x24]; ldr r1,[r1]; str r1,[r4]`. svc 0x23 is svcCloseHandle throughout this binary (see 0x00547884, 0x00519224). Callers: 0x00107B54 (map shared block) and 0x00119BAC.

name: Os_IpcSend2Get2
signature: int Os_IpcSend2Get2(u32 value0, u32 value1, u32* out1, u32* out2)
summary: Sends the fixed IPC request 0x00020080 (command 0x80, two normal parameters) to the session at 0x007AF0D8 and copies two response words out of the thread command buffer. Used while mapping a shared block (see 0x00107B54), where the two words are the mapped base address and size.
evidence: `iVar2 = mrc p15,0,r2,c13,c0,3; iVar2->f_80 = g_0010dc20 (=0x00020080); f_84 = arg1; f_88 = arg2; result = *g_0010dc24 (handle 0x007AF0D8); svc #0x32; if (result >= 0) { *out1 = f_8c; *out2 = f_90; result = f_84; }`. 0x00020080 decodes as command 0x80 with two normal params in the 3DS IPC header layout.

name: Os_IpcSendGetHandle
signature: int Os_IpcSendGetHandle(u32* outHandle, u32 value0, u32* out2, u32* out3)
summary: Same svcSendSyncRequest shape with request 0x00010040 (command 0x40, one normal parameter). Besides two plain words it copies the handle the kernel placed at command-buffer +0x94 into *outHandle, i.e. this is the 'allocate and hand me the kernel object' request of the SDK memory path.
evidence: `f_80 = g_0010dc7c (=0x00010040); f_84 = arg2; result = *g_0010dc80 (=0x007AF0D8); svc #0x32; if (result >= 0) { *out2 = f_88; *out3 = f_8c; *outHandle = f_94; result = f_84; }`. Only caller: 0x00107B54, which immediately stores the returned handle via 0x0010CF40 and derives two capability flags from *out3.

name: maybe_Os_IpcSendByte
summary: Sends request 0x00550040 (command 0x40 with twenty-one normal parameters) carrying a single byte, and returns the response word. Called at the end of the heap/shared-block bootstrap with 0, which reads like a 'finish setup' flag.
evidence: `f_80 = g_0010dd8c (=0x00550040); f_84 = arg1; result = *g_0010dd90 (=0x007AF0D8); svc #0x32; if (ok) result = f_84;`. Caller: 0x00102894 (heap creation), with 0 after the block has been mapped.

name: Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen
summary: Makes sure the SDK session described by 0x007AF0BC is open: if the open flag is set it retries svcSendSyncRequest until it succeeds (resetting the handle on failure and re-opening it once), otherwise it opens the session by name with 0x001192C0(handle, name, strlen(name), 0). Errors are fatal and reported through 0x00118924.
evidence: `pcVar1 = g_0010def4 (0x007AF0BC); iVar5 = g_0010def8 (0xE0A0CFF9); iVar7 = *g_0010defc (handle ptr 0x007AF0D8); if (*pcVar1 != 0) { ... if (iVar7 == 0) { uVar4 = strlen_of(name at pcVar1+8); iVar5 = func_001192C0(handlePtr, name, uVar4, 0); } ... }` and the else branch does the same open once. 0x0011CCA0 is strlen (classic ARM `uqsub8` word-at-a-time scanner at 0x0011CCA0), and 0x001192C0 is the srv 'get service handle' call (same shape as 0x00107024 which passes the "dsp::DSP" literal 0x0072FBC0).

name: Mem_InitRangeAllocator
signature: void Mem_InitRangeAllocator(u32* desc, u32 base, u32 size)
summary: Initialises a simple bump/range descriptor: zeroes the six bookkeeping words, then stores base at +0 and base+size at +4 - the allocator used for the application heap window measured by Mem_ComputeLinearHeapRange. The critical section at +0xC is (re)initialised every call.
evidence: `desc[2]=desc[3]=desc[4]=desc[5]=desc[1]=desc[0]=0; ... if (empty) { func_00111E28(desc+3); desc[1] = base + size; desc[0] = base; }`. Its only caller is 0x00106F94, passing 0x007F2B88 and (0x0E000000, top-0x0E000000). The same descriptor shape (base, end) is consumed by the heap code as a free range.

name: maybe_Snd_ResetMixingState
summary: Resets one mixing unit: re-initialises the critical section at +0x2C, points the two voice tables at +0x38/+0x6C, sets the volume field to 0x20 and both pan/gain pairs to unity (0x7FFF), clearing them with the exclusive-access spin loop the atomic helpers use.
evidence: Body: func_00111E28(&self->f_2c); self->f_38 = self+0x6c; f_58 = 0x20; f_5c = f_60 = 0; then five `do { } while (!hasExclusiveAccess(...))` blocks zeroing f_64, f_68, f_3c, f_40/f_42 = 0x7fff, f_44, f_48/f_4a = 0x7fff; func_00111E28(&self->f_4c). Caller 0x005422AC is in the sound engine block (0x0054xxxx, see 0x005428EC/0x00549A70).

name: maybe_Snd_InitMixingState
signature: void maybe_Snd_InitMixingState(SndMixState* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Same structure layout as 0x00110DEC but takes the two table pointers/sizes from the caller: stores them at +0/+8, clears the counters and both gain pairs (0x7FFF), and initialises the critical section at +0x38.
evidence: Mirror image of 0x00110DEC on the same offsets (f_38/f_3c/f_40/f_42/f_44/f_48/f_4a, 0x7fff fills). Callers 0x00108C5C and 0x0054B608 are both inside the audio engine region.

name: maybe_Snd_LoadArchiveFromReader
signature: int maybe_Snd_LoadArchiveFromReader(void* self, Reader* reader, int poolCountA, int poolCountB, u32 arg5, u32 capacity, int wantData)
summary: Loads an archive/resource through a random-access reader: reads and validates a 0x28-byte header, checks that capacity covers poolCountA*0x20 + poolCountB*0x18, then builds two fixed-record pools (0x20-byte records at +0xB8, 0x18-byte records at +0xF4) on top of the reader's data, wires four table descriptors into the object and finally registers the reader in one of five slots chosen by the object's category value. Best guess for the domain is the SDK audio archive layer; the record semantics themselves are unconfirmed.
evidence: `result = (**(code**)*arg2)(arg2, &out, 0, 0, buf, 0x28); if (out != 0x28) return 0xC8A04554;` then `arg3 = poolCountA * 0x20; ... uVar2 = arg3 + poolCountB * 0x18 + extra; if (capacity < uVar2) return 0xD8604659;` (both error codes are the literals at 0x001118CC/0x001118D0), `func_00118A88(&self->f_b8, 0x20, arg5, arg3, 4, 0)`, `func_00118A88(&self->f_f4, 0x18, arg5+arg3, poolCountB*0x18, 4, 0)`, then a five-way `*(u32**)(self + category*4 + 0xc) = reader`. Tail: func_00117078(self+4) (an IPC request) with error report at 0x0011187C.

name: maybe_Snd_LoadArchiveTailArm
summary: Second entry point into the archive loader 0x001114F4: only the tail (pool setup + reader registration + IPC request) is reproduced, because the code is entered with register arguments the decompiler could not attribute. Kept as its own symbol because it is used as a call target.
evidence: Ghidra shows `unaff_r4/r5/r6/r7/r8/r9/r10` plus `in_stack_...` arguments; the body from `unaff_r4->f_3c = unaff_r9` onwards is statement-for-statement the tail of 0x001114F4 (same func_00118A88(&f_b8,0x20), func_00118A88(&f_f4,0x18,...), func_00117078(r+4), same five-way slot selection at +0xc). No callers in the readable tree.

name: maybe_Snd_LoadArchiveTailThumb
signature: u32 maybe_Snd_LoadArchiveTailThumb(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Thumb-mode twin of 0x00111C58: same loader tail, entered with four arguments (the last one is the byte-swapped pool size used for the first pool). Registered as an entry point because ARM/Thumb interworking reaches it directly.
evidence: Mode 'thumb' in the seed table; identical tail to 0x001114F4 including `func_00118A88(&unaff_r4->f_b8, 0x20)` and the five-way category slot write at +0xc; it does the `(arg1<<24 | ...)` byte swap that the ARM version performs on a value it loads from memory.

name: Os_InitCriticalSection
summary: Initialises one recursive critical section: clears the owner thread and the recursion counter at +4/+8. 32 call sites, always right after an object has been zeroed or allocated, and always paired with Os_CriticalSectionEnter (0x00117E50) / leave (0x00117ED0).
evidence: Body: `func_00117C40(); *(u32*)(cs+4) = 0; *(u32*)(cs+8) = 0;`. 0x00117E50 compares `mrc p15,0,r1,c13,c0,3` (the current thread pointer) against cs+4, re-locks and increments cs+8 - the classic recursive-lock owner/count pair; 0x00117E88 releases it and clears the owner when the count reaches zero. 32 callers, all object constructors (e.g. 0x0010C738, 0x001114F4, 0x005428EC).

name: Os_InitThreadLocalStorage
summary: Fills in the thread-local block of the calling thread: points the TLS table at +0x5C/+0x64/+0x68 at the per-thread storage, publishes the TLS destructor table, and resolves the per-thread data pointer (0x001000B8) so that thread-local destructors can run at thread exit.
evidence: `iVar1 = mrc p15,0,r0,c13,c0,3; iVar1->f_5c = &iVar1->f_60; iVar1->f_64 = g_00111f54; iVar1->f_68 = g_00111f58; f_60 = f_6c = f_70 = f_74 = f_78 = 0; iVar1->f_7c = (g_00111f50 == 0) ? 0 : func_001000B8();`. 0x001181B8 then walks 16 TLS slots and calls the registered destructor for each with the thread's slot value - the pair is the TLS manager.

name: maybe_Snd_EnsureStateInitialised
summary: Lazy 'initialise once' guard for the sound-system state: if the flag byte is clear it initialises the critical section at +0x34 and sets the flag. Called by Snd_InitSystemState before it touches the block.
evidence: `if (*arg1 == 0) { func_00111E28(arg1 + 0x34); *arg1 = 1; }`; single caller 0x0010C738 (Snd_InitSystemState), which passes the .bss singleton 0x007F2C3C.

name: maybe_Snd_SetOutputMode
summary: Stores the speaker configuration byte at +2 of the sound state and forwards it to the mixing layer under the global sound lock; returns 0 when the lock could not be taken.
evidence: `func_0011E99C(); if (func_0011E9B4()) { *(char*)(self+2) = mode; result = func_00119140(g_00112de4 (0x007EF414), mode); func_0011E9A8(); return result; } func_0011E9A8(); return 0;` - 0x0011E99C/0x0011E9A8/0x0011E9B4 are the sound layer's lock/unlock/trylock triple (used by 30+ sound setters such as 0x00118B58 "set unit level"). Caller 0x0010C738 stores the 3DS output mode (0/1/2).

name: Os_InitSrvClient
summary: Brings up the srv client at boot: initialises the memory manager, then opens the "srv:" port (name string at 0x00741AD8) with a retry loop that keeps retrying while the result is 'session closed', and finally sends the srv handshake request (0x00107800) once. Returns the last result code.
evidence: `func_00106F70(); if (*g_00113538 == 0) { ...init...; *g = 1; } func_00117E50(lock); ... while (1) { uVar5 = func_001169C4(g_0011354c, 0x00741AD8 /* "srv:" */, arg3, arg4, ...); if (level != -5) break; if (module != 4 || desc != 0x3fa) break; func_0011CC94(0x0007A120, 0); } if (ok) { uVar5 = func_00107800(); count++; }`. g_00113544 = 0x3FA is the error description the loop retries on (module 4, i.e. the srv module) and g_00113550 = 0x0007A120 (500000 ns) is the retry delay. g_00113540 = 0x00741AD8 is the "srv:" string. Called directly by ResetVector, so it is the first service the CRT brings up.

name: Os_InitMainThreadTls
summary: Prepares the thread-local storage for the main thread (0x00111EB0 then 0x00111EFC) and returns the default application heap size 0x03000000 (48 MB) that the caller hands to the heap setup.
evidence: Body is three statements: func_00111EB0(); func_00111EFC(); return 0x3000000; - i.e. the same TLS pair as 0x0011CC30's thread trampoline. Its only caller 0x00106F70 passes the return value straight to 0x0010BDB0, which is the heap-size commit.

name: maybe_Os_SendServiceInitRequest
summary: Sends the service 'initialise' request 0x08630000 (command 0, three normal and three handle parameters) using the handle stored at *handle, so it registers a set of kernel objects with the service. Called at the end of every archive load in this region.
evidence: `local_10 = func_00117098(); func_0011DED4(&local_10, arg1);` and 0x0011DED4 does `f_80 = g_0011df08 (=0x08630000); result = *arg1; svc #0x32; if (ok) { *arg2 = f_88; result = f_84; }`. 0x08630000 decodes as command 0 with three normal and three translate parameters - the standard service-initialise shape. Callers: 0x001114F4 / 0x00111C58 / 0x00111C72 (archive loader) which check the result and abort through 0x0011ED40.

name: maybe_Os_LookupParamEntry
summary: Reads a 0x40-byte header block through the table reader and searches its four 0x10-byte entries for the first one with type byte 0; when found it unpacks two 12-bit fields from the entry's first word, copies the two payload words, and fills out[1] with a 1.0f default. Falls back to the scan in 0x0011E0DC and then to a fixed default (0x800 / 0x800 / 1.0f) when nothing matches.
evidence: `result = func_001223B0(0x00?, &local_18, 0, 0x40); iVar3 = 3; do { puVar4 = (u32*)(table + iVar3*0x10); if ((*puVar4 & 0xff) == 0) { copy 15-byte name via 0x001232F8; if (match) { out[1] = ((*p << 12) >> 20); out[3] = (*p >> 20); *out = p[1]; iVar5 = p[2]; } } } while (iVar3-- >= 0); if (no match) { if (0x0011E0DC(out) < 0) { out defaults 0x800/0x800/0x3F800000; } }`. The 0x800 defaults and the 1.0f scale are the classic centre/scale pair of a calibration record, but the record's consumer is not visible here, hence the low confidence.

name: Os_RunTlsDestructors
summary: Runs the thread-local destructors for the thread that has just finished: walks the 16 destructor slots, and for each slot that is both present in the thread's mask and non-null it calls destructor(thread->slot[i]). Called by the thread trampoline immediately before svcExitThread.
evidence: `mask = g_00118208; table = g_00118204; for (i = 0; i < 0x10; i++) { pc = table[i]; if (i < 0x10 && ((*mask >> i) & 1) && pc != 0) { tp = mrc p15,0,r0,c13,c0,3; pc(tp[i]); } }`; caller 0x0011CC30 = the thread entry trampoline (its next call is svc #9, svcExitThread).

name: Os_InitializeOnce
summary: Classic one-shot initialisation with a published state: the first caller atomically flips the flag from 0 to 1, initialises the global object 0x007EF0A4 and then stores its address in the flag (state 2); every other caller sleeps 1 ms until the flag reaches 2. Returns the published pointer/state.
evidence: `do { uVar3 = *flag; if (uVar3 != 0) { ClearExclusiveLocal(); goto done; } } while (!hasExclusiveAccess(flag)); *flag = 1;` then `if (uVar3 == 0) { *g_001184e8 = 0; func_00111E28(g_001184e8); ...; *flag = (u32)puVar2; } else { while (*flag < 2) func_0011CC94(0x000F4240 /* 1e6 ns = 1 ms */, 0); }`. g_001184ec = 0x000F4240 is that sleep argument.

name: Mem_InitBlockPool
signature: void Mem_InitBlockPool(Pool* self, int blockBytes, int usedBytes, int totalBytes, int align, u32 flags)
summary: Turns a raw buffer into a pool of fixed-size blocks: computes the aligned block stride, the block count and the first/last block addresses, then links every block into a singly linked free list and records head/tail. No allocation happens here - the caller supplies the memory.
evidence: `self->f_14 = flags; iVar1 = align_up(blockBytes, align) * align; self->f_18 = iVar1; n = align_up(usedBytes, align); self->f_1c = n * align; blocks = align_up(usedBytes + totalBytes - self->f_1c, iVar1); self->f_20 = blocks * iVar1; ... do { *p = prev; p -= self->f_18; } while (p >= self->f_1c); self->f_24 = p;` - the loop writes each block's 'next' pointer, so f_24 is the free-list head. Called with (0x20 block, ...) and (0x18 block, ...) by the archive loader 0x001114F4.

name: maybe_Os_WaitSharedBlock
summary: Waits for the shared-block handle stored in *state with svcWaitSynchronization1 (svc 0x24), asserts on a negative result, and then makes sure the SDK session is open again (0x0010DDCC). Looks like the 'wait for the mapping/transfer to finish' half of the shared-block handling done by 0x00107B54.
evidence: `if (*arg1 != 0) { software_interrupt(0x24); if (*arg1 < 0) func_00118100(); } func_0010DDCC();` - svc 0x24 is svcWaitSynchronization1 (same immediate read by batch N_080 at 0x00105704), 0x00118100 is the fatal-error path and 0x0010DDCC re-opens the session. No callers in the readable tree; reached through a function pointer.

name: Os_ThreadEntry
summary: Entry point of every created thread: sets up the thread-local storage, calls the two function pointers the thread was started with (start->callback(start->arg) then start->main(arg)), runs the thread-local destructors, and finishes with svcExitThread (svc 9).
evidence: Ends with `bl 0x1181b8` (Os_RunTlsDestructors), `ldr r0,[r4,#0x10]; cmp r0,#0; blne 0x11699c`, `pop {r4,lr}`, `svc #9`, `bx lr`. The two indirect calls read `[r4+4]`/`[r4+0xc]` and `[r4]`/`[r4+0xc]`, i.e. fn(arg) pairs. 0x0011CB38 in the same block is the 'current context' getter used by 994 call sites.

name: maybe_Os_IpcServiceInitWithHandle
summary: Sends the fixed request 0x08630000 (command 0, three normal and three handle parameters) using *handle as the session and copies one response word to *out. Thin variant of 0x00117078 without the argument shuffling.
evidence: `iVar2 = mrc p15,0,r0,c13,c0,3; iVar2->f_80 = g_0011df08 (=0x08630000); result = *arg1; svc #0x32; if (result >= 0) { *arg2 = iVar2->f_88; result = iVar2->f_84; }`. Single caller: 0x00117078.

name: maybe_Os_ScanParamBlocks
summary: Fallback scan for the parameter/calibration table: reads sixteen 0x40-byte blocks starting at file offset 0x400, looks in each for an entry whose type byte is 0xFE, and on a hit unpacks the same two 12-bit fields and two payload words as 0x001179C0. Returns the fixed error code 0xE7E3FFFF when nothing matches.

Note the 16-bit offset wrap, i.e. a small table read through a windowed reader.

name: Os_ReadChunkedTable
signature: int Os_ReadChunkedTable(Reader* reader, int* bytesRead, int offset, u32 size)
summary: Reads up to `size` bytes through a reader in at most 0x40-byte requests, adding the wrapped 16-bit current offset each time, and accumulates how many bytes were transferred. It is the small-block reader the parameter-table lookups use.

name: Battle_UpdateEncounterTransition
summary: Per-frame driver of the battle-encounter transition, reachable from the script native EncountEventEx. On frame 1 it rebuilds the 0x1348-byte transition object from its static template (copying 0xDC bytes over a zeroed block) and resets two flags in the game singletons; on later frames it compares the frame counter against half the active screen extent minus 15 and, at the matching frames, flips the two 2D layers through their vtable entry +0x28. Returns 1 once the transition is over - that return value is what ends the script's frame loop.
evidence: Squirrel caller (game_assets/scripts/packs/script/base/script.decompiled.nut): `for (local frame = 0; EncountEventEx(battleID, false, frame) == false; ++frame) suspend(1);` and EncountEventEx passes its third argument straight to this function (EncountEventEx_0014da1c.c line 50). Body: one-time build guarded by the flag at 0x0015E0E4 - `size = align(0x1348, 0x10); memset(block, 0x1348); *block = vtable 0x0015E0FC; memcpy(block+4, 0x005329E0, 0xdc, 3)`; the two half-extents come from `(int)(self->f_11a0 * 0.5f) - 0xf` and `(int)(self->f_119c * 0.5f) - 0xf` with 0.5f = the literal at 0x0015E498; the layer toggles are `(**(code**)(*(*(ptr+0x14)+0x10) + 0x28))(ptr,0,1)` and the +0x1c variant, where the object comes from func_006F229C, which sibling batch N_021 names Ui_GetCore. The two game-singleton fields it resets are Os_GetGameWork()+0x74 and +0x78 (0x006F1EEC, N_077). Other callers 0x003686B8/0x00368704 are the same battle-transition helpers.

name: Snd_RequestEncounterSound
summary: Selects and requests the sound for an encounter/battle: looks the battle id up in two game tables (0x0063CC1C then 0x0063D9BC), and only when the resulting id differs from the one the sound player is currently using does it stop the old sound (0x001EE220) and request the new one (0x001EC1D0). The id is a small table value (< 0x9E) and is played back through the sound player's request queue, so this is the battle BGM / monster battle sound selection, not a script-level call.
evidence: Called from EncountEventEx with the battle id whenever the encounter is a normal one. Body: `e = func_0063CC1C(*ctx, battleId); if (e && e[5] != 0xff) { r = func_0063D9BC(*ctx, e[5]); if (r) id = r[8]; }` then `cur = (snd[4] & 2) ? snd[0x64] : snd[0x58]; if (cur != id) { func_001EE220(); func_001EC1D0(snd, id); }`. `snd` comes from func_006F1DF8, which sibling batch N_077 names Sound_GetPlayer; 0x001EC1D0 queues an id into the 64-entry ring at +0x1848 (rejects ids >= 0x9E) and 0x001EE220 flushes it. N_032 independently proposed Snd_RequestBgmPlay for 0x001EC1D0, which is consistent but not proven, hence the neutral 'sound' wording.

Called from EncountEventEx for non-default encounters and from 0x001A14EC / 0x0046E50C / 0x004AE8C4.

name: maybe_Event_ReleaseCapturedObject
summary: Releases the object captured at +0x3DC: calls the third slot of its vtable (the 'release/detach' entry) with a scratch handle, then marks +0x3D8 as 'already released'. Runs when an event has been caught so the pending reference does not survive into the next frame.

name: Script_BindUiMessageNatives
summary: Registers the 73 UI / message / talk natives into the Squirrel root table: window control (StartUI, EndUI, IsMenuActive, StartTutorialUI), message setup and query (ScriptMessageSetup, ScenarioMessageSetup, IEMessageSetup, MessageFunc, FukidashiMessage, SpiritMessage, DialogOpen, GetDialogResult), message arguments, quest stamps, hope/soul/yocchi selection, party talk, picture cards, the casino jackpot queries and ChangeUIMap.

SetActionInputEnable). 0x006BC528 is the native-method binder (see its entry). Called from the class-registration table at 0x00253EF8 via 0x005799F4.

name: Script_RegisterThread
signature: void Script_RegisterThread(GameObject* self, u32 nameKey, u32 funcRef)
summary: Adds one script thread object to the game object's thread list: builds a Squirrel reference to the closure, appends a 0x14-byte entry (vtable, key, reference, flag) to the growable array at +0x3F0, and stores the value under the given key in the VM table. This is the C++ side of the script function RegistThread().
evidence: Only caller is RegistThread (0x0014A778), which resolves the game object and calls this with the script arguments. The code is a byte-for-byte twin of 0x00250A38 (same prologue, same 0x14-byte element growth including the `(count/0x14)*2` resize, same func_00579D98 / func_006BC724 / func_006BC7A0 / func_006BB664 / func_006BBCEC sequence).
